notes: Matched 85 of 88 coder A units and 99 coder B units by passage and rule; coder A units 88, coder B 99. Main disagreement kinds: (1) policy_type between neighboring types for the same passage (P66/P09 for 'communicate your expectations', P37/P81 for the misuse protocol, P50/P77 for the data-handling sentence, P56/P73 for human-centered design, P31/P53/P98 for human-in-the-loop, P04/P09 for the UA instructor sentence, P36/P95 for 'do not cheat', P87/P44 and P70/P72); each was settled by re-reading the sentence and choosing the type whose definition matches what the sentence regulates, with the other coder's concern kept in fit_note. (2) Modality and phase for advisory or informational sentences (invitations, news blurbs, 'make sure to', 'avoid'): imperatives and invitations were coded should/should-not, descriptions informs. (3) unit_stance for verification, compliance and incident-response duties (A neutral, B restrict): neutral, because these conditions do not ban or narrow AI use. (4) Actor for statements with no addressee (all) versus statements aimed at instructors. (5) Unit boundaries: coder A merged some adjacent items (blindspots + opposing views; two sentences on data and human-in-the-loop) which were split, and one sentence with two rules (units may add requirements but may not weaken the baseline) was split into two units. Single-coder units: coder A only 3 (1 kept, 2 dropped as rhetorical questions with no position); coder B only 14 (12 kept after checking the source, 2 dropped: an opening clause 'Whatever your course policy is' with a policy that went beyond the text, and a duplicate P11 unit of the paraphrase sentence). Final units: 99 (85 matched, 1 kept A-only, 12 kept B-only, 1 added by splitting a two-rule sentence). Document stances all agreed (delegates, permit, delegates). Topic codes outside the AGENT_BRIEF starter list were used by both coders (for example governance, verification-accuracy, faculty-support, faculty-course-materials) and are kept as written.
